0.long_answer: Mutations in the BBS1 gene are associated with Bardet-Biedl syndrome type 1. Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) is genetically heterogeneous, meaning that mutations in several different genes (BBS1 through BBS7, among others) can cause the disorder. The BBS1 gene, in particular, is responsible for one form of the syndrome and is typically referred to as Bardet-Biedl syndrome type 1. This specific subtype is characterized by the typical signs of BBS, which can include retinal dystrophy, obesity, polydactyly, renal anomalies, and cognitive impairment. Research has identified a common mutation, M390R, in the BBS1 gene that plays a major role in the development of this form of the disease.
